chapters.reason: The paper proposes Sketch-of-Thought (SoT) to reduce token usage in reasoning by using cognitively inspired paradigms and linguistic constraints, which aligns with explicit length budgeting via prompt-based constraints and concise intermediate steps, operating purely at inference time.

SoT dynamically selects among three reasoning paradigms (Conceptual Chaining, Chunked Symbolism, Expert Lexicons) based on task complexity via a lightweight router, resembling a System 1/System 2 switch within a single framework, though not explicitly framed as dual-process theory.

The method compresses reasoning chains into shorter, sketch-like outputs to reduce verbosity, which is analogous to reasoning chain compression by producing explicit but concise text tokens, though it is implemented via prompting rather than supervised fine-tuning.
